2.text: Some of the Chukchee say that ochre comes from the vaˊɪrg̣ɪt, and

3.text: graphite from the keˊlet. Thus, in one tale, a boy and a girl, coming home

4.text: from a long journey, are painted, — the boy with ochre, and the girl

5.text: with graphite. The former lives, but the latter dies.

6.text: The marks used by the Maritime Chukchee on these occasions are a

7.text: simple combination of dots and lines, and are quite similar to those described

8.text: as found among the Reindeer Chukchee.

9.text: A sample of the marks made with graphite, and in use among the

10.text: Asiatic Eskimo and the inhabitants of the Diomede Islands, is given in Fig. 260.

33.text: Masks. — I am not aware of any use of masks in the ceremonials of

34.text: either the Chukchee or the Asiatic Eskimo. I found, indeed, among the

35.text: Maritime Chukchee, a couple of masks made of reindeer-skin (Fig. 262), which

36.text: were called “hairy face” (rɪnɪluˊᵋ), after the manner of the Koryak, who call

37.text: their wooden masks, used in performances of a somewhat ceremonial character,

38.text: “wooden face.” The “hairy faces” of the Chukchee, however, have no con-

39.text: nection with their ceremonials, at least not at the present time. According
